blocks.orig: 4-day Tanzania Safari extension: two northern parks
blocks.html: 4-day safari extension in Tanzania: two parks in the north

blocks.orig: Whether you are planning to climb Mount Kilimanjaro or live your best life on Zanzibar, this safari extension is perfect to make your trip to Tanzania complete. Together with a private guide, you will explore two beautiful national parks in northern Tanzania: the Ngorongoro Crater and the Tarangire National Park.
blocks.html: Whether you plan to climb Mount Kilimanjaro or want to make the most of your time on Zanzibar, this safari extension rounds off your trip to Tanzania nicely. With a private guide you discover two beautiful national parks in the north of Tanzania: the Ngorongoro Crater and the Tarangire National Park.

blocks.orig: Ngorongoro Crater is home to the highest concentration of wildlife in Africa and one of the world’s best destinations to spot Africa’s Big Five. For elephant lovers, the Tarangire National Park is hard to beat. Explore the African wilderness under majestic Baobab trees and meet the largest congregation of wild elephants on the planet.
blocks.html: The Ngorongoro Crater has the highest concentration of wildlife in Africa and is one of the best places in the world to see Africa’s Big Five. If you love elephants, the Tarangire National Park is hard to top. Discover the African wilderness beneath impressive Baobab trees and see the largest gathering of wild elephants on earth.

blocks.orig: This private Tanzania safari offers you the flexibility to travel at your own pace with a private safari vehicle and knowledgeable, English-speaking guide.
blocks.html: On this private Tanzania safari you are free to travel at the pace you prefer, with your own safari vehicle and a well-informed guide who speaks English.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: On a safari with us you get the chance to discover Tanzania’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is yours alone. You choose when each safari day begins and finishes, and our experienced guides are happy to help you decide on the day itself. Perhaps you want to see the animals when they are most active around sunrise and sunset, when it is pleasantly cool, or perhaps you would rather finish the afternoon at the pool: the choice is yours. Because animals in Tanzania are active at different times of day, you will have many chances to see them in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. Lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo can all be seen in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is a safe and friendly country for travellers. You will find a hospitable atmosphere, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, and you can enjoy the scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. People are welcoming, and as anywhere else in the world it is sensible to take normal precautions, such as watching your belongings. With its natural beauty and warm people, Tanzania is a wonderful country to visit.

blocks.orig: As you walk out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide greets you with a big smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' The guide takes you straight to your hotel, where you can relax and take in the African atmosphere. The next day your guide takes you on an exclusive, private safari that allows you to travel at your own pace. Enjoy the luxury of your own safari jeep and take the liberty to stop and watch the animals as long as you like!
blocks.html: When you step out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide is waiting with a broad smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' You are driven directly to your hotel, where you can unwind and soak up the African atmosphere. The following day your guide sets off with you on an exclusive, private safari, so you can travel at the pace that suits you. You have your own safari jeep, and you are free to stop and watch the animals for as long as you want.

blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Large groups of elephants and a great many giant baobab trees are what Tarangire National Park is known for. The baobabs can live for hundreds of years, and in the dry season elephants actually use them as a water source, drawing water from them with a special technique. In the dry season the Tarangire River is also the only source of water, so at that time of year you can see groups of up to 250 elephants in Tarangire, along with many other animals!

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The well-known Ngorongoro Crater is counted among Africa's seven natural wonders. It was created two million years ago when a huge volcano erupted. The fertile lava produced a unique ecosystem that is now home to the highest concentration of animals anywhere in Africa! Inside the crater you are surrounded by thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, and the views are so striking you won’t know where to look first!

blocks.orig: The last day! Depending on your flight time, you can relax in the lodge a bit longer before heading to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for your flight home. Having second thoughts? It's also possible to add a few days to your holiday by going to one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
